raw_response:
Looking at my situation and what I know from farming this land my whole life:

I have about 12 mu of contracted land. My father farmed it, I farm it, that is how things are done here. Everyone in the village plants winter wheat and summer corn — the same rotation my family has done for as long as I can remember. The government seed stations pushed hybrid corn seeds years ago and the yields were better, so I switched. For wheat I use the improved varieties the village seed shop sells — I do not know the names well but I buy what the shop recommends and what my neighbors use.

Water is the main worry. The groundwater level drops every year, I can feel it in how long the pump runs. But I still irrigate the same number of times I always have — the wheat needs it, especially before the dry spring winds hit. Four times for wheat, two times for corn.

For fertilizer, I buy the compound bags at the co-op and then add urea on top at jointing stage for wheat and before tasseling for corn. I probably put on more than needed but I am afraid of a bad yield. A bad year means I cannot afford the next season's inputs.

I do rotary tillage before wheat planting after I harvest the corn stalks. For corn, I just direct seed into the wheat stubble — saves time, everyone does it now.
